scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “The curve scaling limit of half-plane double dimers” (preprints/The-curve-scaling-limit-of-half-plane-double-dimers-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 226 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2e1bcd39145db94c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the half-plane Temperleyan law specified above, the family F(Lδ) is tight as δ ↓ 0 in the loop-collection topology just defined, and F(Lδ) =⇒ F(L), δ ↓ 0, where L is standard nested CLE4 in H. The convergence holds along the full mesh limit and matches all macroscopic loops as curves.
